title: This Deep-Sea Crab Farms Its Own Food on Its Hairy Claws

scenes.text: This crab farms its own food on its arms.
It's a yeti crab, living by methane seeps on the ocean floor off Costa Rica.
Its claws and body hairs are covered in a garden of bacteria.
It waves its claws over the seeps, which scientists think feeds the bacteria fresh chemicals.
Then it scrapes the bacteria off with comb-like mouthparts and eats them.

description:
This crab farms its own food on its arms.
The yeti crab Kiwa puravida grows bacteria on its hairy claws near methane seeps off Costa Rica, then eats them.
Would you eat a crop that grows on your own arms?
